meaning:
δῆλος, -η, -ον
[in LXX for אוּר, etc. ;]
1. visible.
2. clear to the mind, evident: Mat.26:73; δ. (sc. ἐστίν), before ὅτι, 1Co.15:27, Gal.3:11.†
SYN.: φανερός, with ref. to outward appearance, manifest as opposite to concealed; δ. with ref. to inner perception, evident, known, under­stood. (AS)

elsewhere.note: After a little while those who stood by came and said to Peter, “Surely you are also one of them, for your speech makes you known.”
For, “He put all things in subjection under his feet.” But when he says, “All things are put in subjection”, it is evident that he is excepted who subjected…
Now that no man is justified by the law before God is evident, for, “The righteous will live by faith.”
